title: Capacity prioritization scorecard & SLA negotiation log for enterprise Dedicated requests
creator: Maya Patel
description: Purpose: Create a repeatable, defensible scorecard and negotiation checklist for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that maps customer needs (throughput, latency SLO, data isolation) to recommended GPU classes, reserved throughput profiles, and scaling policies. This ticket captures the final rubric, decision log from the customer workshop on 2025-02-24, recommended default mappings, and a short negotiation script for sales/solutions engineering to use during intake.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A one-page scorecard that turns customer answers into a recommended reserved throughput profile and GPU class. 2) A documented decision log of edge cases and trade-offs (e.g., latency vs cost for multi-tenant workloads). 3) A sales negotiation checklist with fallback guarantees (model variant swap, regional fallback) and template SLA language. 4) Hand-off notes to ENG and Solutions for implementation and onboarding.
recommendations_summary: - Default mapping: small bursty customers -> T4x2 with aggressive autoscale; steady high-throughput text-generation -> A10x4 or H100x2 depending on per-token latency targets. - Latency SLO tiers: Gold (<150ms p95), Silver (150-300ms p95), Bronze (>300ms p95). Map Gold to pinned low-batch nodes + KV cache warmup policies. - Reserved throughput profiles: define Baseline (10k tok/s), Steady (50k tok/s), High (200k tok/s). Associate each profile with expected GPU class and autoscale buffer. - Autoscaling policy recommendation: combine CPU/GPU utilization with request queue depth and model size signals; prefer vertical scaling (more streams per GPU) for cost-sensitive customers, horizontal scaling for strict p95 latency targets.
tradeoffs_and_notes: - Cost vs latency: Gold SLOs require reserved capacity and potentially higher-cost GPU classes; present customers with delta pricing. - Model compatibility: quantized variants reduce GPU class needs but may introduce quality regressions; include QA gate for each model variant. - Regional capacity constraints: if preferred region lacks H100, propose cross-region routing with data residency caveats and SLA adjustments. - Onboarding runway: recommend a 2-week canary with phased traffic ramp and rollback criteria.
